business.overview:
NVIDIA monetizes accelerated computing through GPUs and CPUs, high-speed networking, rack-scale systems, enterprise software and developer libraries. Data Center is a disclosed market platform and generated $89.0B in Q2 FY27; it sits inside Compute & Networking reporting rather than constituting a separate reportable segment.

The AI transmission channel is paid compute. More training, inference and agent workloads require accelerators, memory bandwidth, networking and CUDA-optimized software; Rubin and Spectrum-6 increase NVIDIA content per deployed AI factory rather than merely replacing one GPU generation.

The model breaks if customers digest capacity, shift meaningful workloads to internal ASICs, or cannot secure power and financing. China restrictions, foundry and packaging concentration, and a mistimed platform transition can turn exceptional demand into inventory and margin pressure.

NVIDIA's per-share test is shipment quality: operating cash must keep pace while receivables and inventory expand through Rubin. Equity-investment gains cannot substitute for accelerator, networking and systems profit.

Rubin execution must preserve gross margin while converting inventory and receivables into collected system revenue.
business.moat: CUDA's installed developer base, co-designed compute/networking/software stack and annual platform cadence reduce customer time-to-deployment. The moat is strongest when system performance and software availability matter more than chip price; it weakens if hyperscaler ASICs absorb standardized workloads or interoperability lowers switching costs.

business.overview:
Okta earns subscription revenue from workforce identity and Auth0 customer identity products. Contract value grows through seats, applications, governance modules, privileged access and machine-to-machine usage; cRPO is the cleanest near-term demand measure. Workforce products secure employees and contractors, while Auth0 is embedded by developers inside customer applications.

AI agents create non-human identities that still need discovery, authentication, authorization and policy enforcement. Okta monetizes that expansion only when agent identity products attach to existing contracts and lift cRPO, not when AI appears in product names. Governance and privileged-access modules can increase spend without relying solely on workforce-seat growth.

The model breaks if Microsoft bundles identity more aggressively, customers consolidate platforms, or another security incident damages trust. Slower workforce-seat growth and weak channel execution can also keep revenue near low-double digits despite better margins. Auth0 must preserve developer loyalty while enterprise selling becomes more efficient; otherwise independent identity becomes a premium point solution competing against suite economics.
business.moat: Okta's moat is neutral connectivity across heterogeneous clouds, applications and directories, reinforced by integration breadth and identity-policy switching costs. It is weaker inside Microsoft-standardized estates, where Entra bundling can turn identity from an independent control plane into a suite feature.

Revenue expands as customers send more telemetry and adopt additional products. Customers above $100,000 ARR test whether platform consolidation is broadening spend.

Generative-AI systems increase model calls, distributed services, traces, token metrics and security events. LLM Observability can link quality, latency and cost to application behavior. Datadog loses pricing power if hyperscalers bundle adequate native monitoring or OpenTelemetry lowers switching costs. A 79.5% gross margin funds investment, but near-zero GAAP operating margin means compensation absorbs much of the accounting profit. Growth must remain broad across products and large customers.

business.overview:

The installed database estate anchors renewals and migration, while OCI supplies the fastest growth. RPO captures signed cloud commitments, but recognition depends on delivering capacity over contract terms.

AI demand reaches Oracle through GPU clusters, networking, database access and sovereign cloud regions. OCI revenue rises after campuses obtain power, hardware is installed and customers accept service. Oracle can cross-sell database and applications if utilization earns an adequate return on construction.

The break point is capital intensity. Oracle spent enough in FY2026 to drive free cash flow to negative $23.7B and plans debt plus equity financing for the next build phase. Delayed power, concentrated counterparties, weak utilization or higher funding costs can turn $638B RPO into leverage and dilution before profitable revenue.

business.moat: Oracle's moat combines mission-critical database lock-in, decades of application and support relationships, and deployment across OCI, customer premises and other clouds. business.overview:
SentinelOne sells endpoint, cloud, identity and data security subscriptions through Singularity. Revenue follows new customers, ARR expansion and additional modules. Customers above $100,000 ARR indicate whether the company is moving from smaller endpoint deployments into broader enterprise contracts.

Purple AI can monetize automation by reducing investigation time, correlating security data and guiding response. Revenue appears through paid module attachment, higher ARR and retention, not chatbot usage. Inference and data costs must remain below incremental subscription value for margin to improve.

The franchise can break if Microsoft bundles security, CrowdStrike wins consolidation budgets, or SentinelOne overspends to defend growth. No debt and ample liquidity buy time, but negative 31% GAAP operating margin means equity compensation and losses still transfer value away from existing shares.

The path to durable profitability requires revenue and ARR to outgrow sales expense, cloud-processing costs and compensation simultaneously. A positive adjusted margin is insufficient when the reported loss remains large and enterprise-customer additions trail total ARR growth.
business.moat: SentinelOne's moat rests on autonomous endpoint detection, a unified security data layer and the workflow cost of replacing agents, policies and response automation across an enterprise fleet. Purple AI can deepen analyst dependence. The defense is narrower than platforms bundling identity, email, network and cloud security.
